title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

errors: The printed text reads (d^3 s/ds^3)=0 for the second free-end condition; it should be (d^3 y/ds^3)=0. This is a typographical error in the original, and the derived equation II (α−β−γ=0) is correct for y'''.

The list of boundary conditions is not exhaustive by modern standards. The 'guided' or sliding end (y'=0, y'''=0) is omitted, so the claim that six cases exhaust the possibilities holds only within Euler's three end types.

ideas.what: Classification of beam end conditions into free, simply supported and clamped, each supplying two conditions, and the resulting six combinations up to interchange of the ends
ideas.modern_name: Boundary conditions for the Euler–Bernoulli beam eigenvalue problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744 Additamentum De curvis elasticis) and Daniel Bernoulli (1742–1751); systematized in Rayleigh's Theory of Sound
ideas.where_published: E65 Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I; also Euler's 1770s papers on vibrating rods, including E526

ideas.what: Free–free end conditions at s=0 expressed as linear equations in the coefficients α, β, γ, δ of the general solution
ideas.modern_name: Setting up the characteristic determinant for free–free beam modes (leading to cos ω cosh ω = 1)

ideas.what: Use of a frictionless horizontal plane to remove gravity from the free–free problem

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine enumeration of boundary-condition cases and the setup of the free–free problem. Both are well documented in Euler's earlier work and in the standard history (Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies).
transcription_corrections: In the free-end condition the image indeed shows (d^3 s / d s^3); this is a misprint for (d^3 y/ds^3), and the transcription faithfully reproduces it.
